caption:
🇬🇧 UK Daily Briefing | Thursday, 29 October 2026

1. 💷 Healey raises taxes on banks and landlords to fund £100 handouts
John Healey raised taxes on banks and landlords to fund a £100 winter handout for 20 million families. In a low-key Budget speech, the chancellor blamed 'global economic storms' for higher energy prices and the cost of living crisis.

2. 💼 Official statistics published on visa holder earnings and employment
Statistics for the year ending March 2026 cover visa holders' earnings, employment and income tax. They match Home Office visa records with HMRC PAYE Real Time Information data and include main applicants and dependants.

3. 🎓 Two-year graduate visa planned for 'high-compliance' universities
The government also announced an expansion of the 'high potential individual' visa route to the top 150 global institutions, as part of efforts to attract 'the world's best graduates'.

4. ⚖️ Respect orders to tackle antisocial behaviour come into force
Perpetrators of antisocial behaviour could face tougher restrictions as new respect orders come into force across England and Wales today.

5. ✈️ Over 4 million illegal cigarettes seized at Manchester Airport
Border Force officers seized more than 4 million illegal cigarettes, worth an estimated £2.59 million, during a four-day crackdown at Manchester Airport.

6. 🚭 Scotland bans sale of nicotine products to under-18s
The ban forms part of the Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026.

7. ⚽ Russo hat-trick fires Arsenal to 3-0 win over Benfica
Alessia Russo became England's all-time leading goalscorer in the Women's Champions League with a hat-trick in Arsenal's 3-0 win over Benfica.

8. 👑 King Charles shows off dance moves on second day of Caribbean tour
Earlier in the day, the King paid his respects to the island's fallen servicemen and women.

Sources: Guardian, GOV.UK Home Office, The Independent, BBC Sport, BBC. Stories summarised from UK media reports. Images: Pixabay.
